content: Nutrilite is a brand specializing in vitamins, minerals, and dietary supplements, originally established in 1934 by Dr. Carl F. Rehnborg. The manufacturing of Nutrilite products is currently managed by Access Business Group, a subsidiary of Alticor. These products are distributed globally through Amway and Quixtar Corporations. In certain countries, including Denmark, Finland, Norway, Sweden, Turkey, Australia, and New Zealand, the brand is marketed under the name Nutriway. The founders of Amway began selling Nutrilite products in 1949. By 1972, Amway had acquired a controlling interest in the company and achieved full ownership in 1994. Nutrilite's vitamin and mineral products are distributed exclusively by Quixtar affiliates, referred to as Independent Business Owners (IBOs) in North America, and by Amway IBOs in over 90 other countries and territories. Amway, Quixtar, and Access Business Group are all subsidiaries of Alticor. Nutrilite claims to be the only global vitamin and mineral brand that grows, harvests, and processes plants on its own certified organic farms. However, the company acknowledges that some of its products may include ingredients derived from plants not grown on their own farms. Nutrilite employs advanced farming techniques, including soil solarization, integrated pest management systems, and sustainable agricultural production practices. IBOs have the flexibility to sell Nutrilite products at any price they choose. In 2001, five Nutrilite products became the first dietary supplements to receive certification from NSF International. Nutrilite has also engaged prominent athletes as brand ambassadors. These include Asafa Powell, the 2006 World Male Athlete of the Year and men’s 100m sprint world record holder from Jamaica; Liu Xiang, the 110m men’s hurdles world record holder, Olympic champion, and World Champion from China; Sanya Richards, the 2006 World Female Athlete of the Year from the USA; and Jennifer Stuczynski, the American pole vault champion.
